solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: File perhaps for certain fauna and flora?

parts.note: the word File is a wild (scrambled) form of the word life, so the clue word is what you get from the phrase read as an instruction

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a document might be filed under plants and animals.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'wild' as an anagram signal applied to LIFE, and it produces FILE; 'perhaps' flags that this is one such example.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild animals and plants living naturally are collectively called by this term.

clue.text: Pitch damp — ex-England 'itter gets caught

indicators.note: the hitter is caught, held inside the word for damp, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: damp means wet
Graeme Hick was an England batsman; dropping his aitch, like the apostrophe in 'itter, leaves ICK

explanation.surface: A soggy cricket pitch leads to a former England batsman being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'itter tells you to drop the H from the hitter's name too: Graeme Hick, a former England batsman, loses his H.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the strip of ground between the stumps is the pitch, also called the wicket.

clue.text: Organ fund — for one of its two cathedrals?

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ
a pool is a fund of shared money

explanation.surface: An appeal raises money for one of a city's cathedrals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the city in question famously has two cathedrals, one Anglican and one Roman Catholic, and the clue imagines a fund for one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This English city on the Mersey is known for having both an Anglican and a Catholic cathedral.

clue.text: What may bring lone Scotsmen, hrs wasted?

definitions.text: What may bring lone Scotsmen, hrs wasted?

indicators.note: the letters are wasted, ruined and thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that draws solitary Scots to spend fruitless hours watching a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange LONE, SCOTSMEN and HRS (fifteen letters) to get the answer; the whole clue also describes the legendary creature that has lone watchers wasting hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous elusive beast said to live in a Highland loch draws hopeful watchers for hours.

clue.text: Permanently on the side of the angels

definitions.meaning: permanently means for all time, never to return

definitions.text: on the side of the angels
definitions.meaning: on the side of the angels means acting in a virtuous, beneficial way

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means forever, and also for the benefit of virtue, as angels would act.

clue.text: A girl hugging jolly types from the fleet

indicators.note: hugging means holding close around, so the girl's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
Jollies is old naval slang for the Royal Marines, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A girl embraces some cheerful sailors from the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly types' are not merry people: the Royal Marines are nicknamed the Jollies in naval slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish armada was a great war fleet, and the word means any large fleet of ships.

clue.text: Song (or air) with singer dancing

indicators.note: letters dancing move about, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune performed while the singer dances around.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SONG, OR AIR and SINGER together (fifteen letters); the whole clue describes the nursery rhyme sung while children dance in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: This nursery rhyme is a children's song sung while dancing round in a circle.

clue.text: Affair brings a regret that doesn't end

indicators.note: a word that doesn't end has lost its final letter

parts.note: to regret or grieve is to mourn

explanation.surface: A love affair leaves someone with lingering regret.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, the word names a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: One present in the PM's residence — cunning, not quiet

parts.note: in means at, as in at home
the British Prime Minister lives at Number Ten Downing Street

indicators.note: not means leave out the named piece from the word before it

parts.note: deep can mean cunning, as in a deep one
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone attending a function at Downing Street is sly but never silent.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN is Number 10 Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's home. 'not quiet' removes P from DEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is present at an event is one who attends it.

clue.text: Chummy leader of Tory cabinet?

parts.note: chummy friends are close

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friendly head of the Conservative cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' suggests a government body, but here it is a cupboard; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard, and a cabinet is a piece of storage furniture.

clue.text: City's commanding officer imprisons six

indicators.note: imprisons means locks up inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A city's military chief locks up six people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to a city or town, so civic matters are a city's concerns.

clue.text: Dismissing complaint after game's got lost at home

indicators.note: after places the complaint later in the answer than the pieces before

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game; the 's stands for has
L is the abbreviation for lost in sports results tables
in means at home
gout is a painful medical complaint

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a protest after a team loses a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is the illness GOUT, not a grievance; 'got' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling something out means excluding or dismissing it as a possibility.

clue.text: Being wrong can make one sourer

indicators.note: can make means these letters can be formed into another word by rearranging

explanation.surface: Getting things wrong can make someone more bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or incorrect is described by this adjective.

clue.text: A short tip — use it in the kitchen

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a prong is a pointed tip, as on a fork

explanation.surface: A brief cooking tip to try out in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is not advice but a point, PRONG, cut short to PRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook ties on this garment to protect clothes while working in the kitchen.

clue.text: Agents securing commercial with top model?

parts.note: Kate Moss is a top fashion model
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Advertising agents sign a famous model for a commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agents' suggests advertising, but they are secret agents of an intelligence service.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel's national intelligence service employs secret agents.

clue.text: A daughter in clan is gay

indicators.note: in places the letters within the word for clan

parts.note: a tribe is a clan

explanation.surface: A family member declares that one daughter is gay.
explanation.definitionFit: The old literary term names a lesbian, a woman who is gay.

clue.text: I am overwhelmed by a country's vivacity

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, engulfed inside the other piece

parts.note: a nation is a country
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone feels swamped by a nation's lively spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness and spirit, a synonym for vivacity.

clue.text: A game soldier leading a sort of defence

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so the soldier goes before the final letter

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A brave soldier heads a type of military defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like an adjective meaning brave, but it is POLO.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: This person about to be nabbed by coppers stopping short harangue

indicators.note: being nabbed by means caught and held within, so one piece goes inside the other
stopping short means the word ends early, losing its last letter

parts.note: coppers are police

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for this person is read backwards

parts.note: this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The speaker is about to be arrested by police in the middle of a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the setter's word for this person, and 'stopping short' trims the police before it swallows that reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a strong verbal or written attack, much like a harangue.

clue.text: Turn one's back on company and sulk

parts.note: to pout is to sulk

explanation.surface: Someone walks out on their companions in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is to avoid or abandon a responsibility, turning one's back on it.

clue.text: Huge rug manufactured for one who'd expect red carpet?

parts.note: huge means big
rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: A huge rug made for someone important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a hairpiece; 'manufactured for' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An important person, a VIP, expects red-carpet treatment.

clue.text: Charm of nasty woman engaging partners at table

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the partners go inside the woman

parts.note: a bitch is a spiteful woman
in bridge East and West are partners at the card table

explanation.surface: An unpleasant woman charms the couple at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and West (E, W) play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to charm or enchant someone.

clue.text: The French female cast into empty pit and shot

indicators.note: cast into means thrown inside, so the French word goes within the other piece
an empty word is left with only its outer letters

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is thrown into a hollow and fired at.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot means small lead pellets fired from a gun.

clue.text: Plant with blue spine losing all outer bits

indicators.note: each word loses its outermost letters, leaving only the middle

explanation.surface: A plant with a blue stem stripped of its outer parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flowering plant with tall spikes.

clue.text: Iron member of royal family, not inclusive

indicators.note: not means the named letters are left out of the word

parts.note: a princess is a member of a royal family
INC is the abbreviation for inclusive

explanation.surface: A royal who refuses to be inclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to iron clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat.

clue.text: Numbers of mathematicians getting political support?

parts.note: in maths a power is a number used as an exponent
in maths a base is the number raised to a power

explanation.surface: Mathematicians wonder whether their numbers bring political clout.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician's power base is the group whose support they rely on.

clue.text: Relation facing torment with terrible rage

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the rearranged letters come first
terrible here signals that the letters are mangled into another order

parts.note: to taunt is to torment

explanation.surface: A relative faces teasing with furious anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges RAGE into GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a relation of the family, a relative.

clue.text: Drink makes one weak, endlessly stupid going about

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps the other letter
endlessly means without its last letter

parts.note: silly means stupid

explanation.surface: Drinking makes someone feeble and endlessly foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes one' just links; SILL (SILLY cut short) wraps W.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to drink greedily, and as a noun it is a drink.

clue.text: Make certain animal will go to river

parts.note: an ass is an animal, a donkey
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a donkey will head to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure is to make sure or certain of something.

clue.text: Case put against group of teachers is a joke

indicators.note: put against means placed alongside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a chest is a case or box
NUT is the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: A legal case brought against a teachers' union is laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a legal case, but it is a box; the NUT is the British National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is an old stale joke heard too often.
